explain: A tiny distribution models choosing the next token. Temperature changes its sharpness; real tokenization and sampling remain model-specific.
steps: Convert synthetic logits to probabilities with a stable softmax. || Compare the most likely token and total probability.
name: token-distribution

explain: Compute dot product, lengths, cosine similarity, and Euclidean distance on known vectors so their distinct meanings are visible.
steps: Pair matching coordinates for the dot product. || Divide by nonzero vector lengths for cosine; compute squared coordinate differences for distance.
name: vector-math

explain: This one-query attention calculation assigns more weight to a matching key and mixes the corresponding value vectors. It is one attention operation, not a full transformer.
steps: Take scaled dot products between the query and each key. || Softmax the scores, then use those weights to sum each value coordinate.
name: attention

explain: One squared-error gradient update changes a learned weight; inference then uses the updated weight without changing it.
steps: Predict with weight 1 on x=2 and target 6. || Subtract learning_rate times the gradient and calculate the new prediction and loss.
name: gradient

explain: Confusion counts determine precision and recall; a model can be precise while missing relevant cases. The counts here are synthetic reviewed outcomes.
steps: Divide true positives by predicted positives for precision. || Divide true positives by actual positives for recall and compare with a baseline.
name: classifier-metrics

explain: Split by entity so messages from the same customer do not leak across training and test data. This deterministic fixture is illustrative, not a general splitting strategy.
steps: Assign entities before selecting their rows. || Assert disjoint customer identities across partitions.
name: grouped-split

explain: Set membership models the nested AI, ML, and deep-learning categories while distinguishing NLP as a task domain. The example organizes concepts rather than training a system.
steps: Represent approaches by the categories they belong to. || Inspect why a rules engine can be AI without being a learned neural model.
name: ai-taxonomy

explain: A bi-encoder scores separately computed representations, whereas a cross-encoder scores each query/document pair jointly. The counters expose different inference work, not real model scores.
steps: Count reusable document encodings for a fixed corpus. || Count joint pair evaluations for two new queries.
name: encoder-comparison

explain: A margin loss penalizes a query whose negative is too close to its positive. A hard negative is relevant-looking but incorrect for the task.
steps: Set reviewed positive and negative similarities. || Calculate how far their separation falls short of the required margin.
name: contrastive

explain: A low-rank update can use fewer trainable parameters while weight quantization changes storage precision. These arithmetic estimates omit optimizer, scale, and runtime overhead.
steps: Compare full matrix parameters with two rank-r factors. || Separately compare 16-bit and 4-bit weight storage.
name: lora-quantization

explain: Preference training consumes chosen/rejected examples; retrieval supplies current evidence during a request. Their data flow is different even when used in the same product.
steps: Model a preference pair as training data. || Keep a current source revision in a separate request packet.
name: preference-vs-retrieval

explain: Different retrieval variants add distinct preparation or search stages. This executable plan shows stage composition without claiming to implement those systems.
steps: Define the stages needed for each variant. || Inspect which variant uses an image encoder versus a graph traversal.
name: rag-variants
